name: Six Senses Shaharut
insider_take: This desert sanctuary sits in Israel's remote Negev Desert, where ancient trade routes once connected civilizations and astronomers now gather for some of the world's clearest stargazing.
whats_special: Six Senses Shaharut is built around a natural desert spring - a rare phenomenon in the Negev that has sustained life here for millennia. The property features Israel's first dedicated dark-sky observatory, taking advantage of the region's minimal light pollution. The resort's architecture incorporates rammed earth construction, blending seamlessly with the dramatic desert landscape of ancient craters and sandstone cliffs.
pro_tip: Book during a new moon phase for the most spectacular stargazing experience, and don't miss the guided desert walks at sunrise when the temperature is perfect and wildlife is most active.
dont_miss: The nearby Ramon Crater (Makhtesh Ramon) - the world's largest erosion crater and a UNESCO World Heritage candidate. Take the resort's guided meditation sessions at the ancient Nabatean ruins, or join the resident astronomer for telescope sessions that reveal planets, nebulae, and the Milky Way in extraordinary detail.
pros: Stunning desert location in the Negev with dramatic landscapes
Exceptional wellness facilities and spa treatments
Sustainable luxury with eco-conscious design and practices
Unique stargazing and desert adventure experiences
cons: Remote desert location requires planned transportation
Limited dining options due to secluded setting
